newsitem.title: UK: Shield declines comment on Greig Middleton.
newsitem.headline: Shield declines comment on Greig Middleton.

text.p: Shield Diagnostics Group Plc declined to comment on Monday on whether it would continue to retain Greig Middleton & Co Ltd as its broker.

Recent press comment said Shield might drop its link with Greig Middleton because of irritation over advice on the way information about its key product was handled and on the timing of share sale by the group's board last year.
"There has been much speculation and that is what it has been, speculation," Shield chief executive officer Gordon Hall told a news conference. "It has not been speculation moved by the company."
Despite being repeatedly pressed, however, Hall declined to say whether Greig Middleton would continue as brokers to Shield. Press reports have suggested that UBS could take over the role.

One industry expert who knows Shield well, who declined to be identified, said Shield's board had been advised to sell shareholdings a year ago, just as the group's share price was rising on the back of optimism about its test for Activated factor twelve (AFT), which it believes to be a much more accurate predictor of heart attack potential than cholesterol levels.
He said this led to a sharp drop in the value of Shield shares as other investors took this as a sign of lack of confidence.

There was further controversy in January, when the company published a newsletter on the AFT test which was not initially sent to the stock exchange. The newsletter sparked a strong rise in the company's share price. Managers at Monday's news conference insisted that the newsletter had not contained any information not already in the public domain.
The industry specialist said "a lot of investors have not been getting a straight story" on the AFT test.
